Hi Alyssa — thanks for the heads up. Quick answers up front, then a few clarifying questions: 

- Ballpark: for a ~60% uplift over current committed monthly tokens, we typically propose a stepped uplift with a blended unit price that sits ~8–14% below list depending on term and payment timing.
- Minimum uplift: no formal minimum beyond the incremental monthly commit, but discounts tie to the incremental committed run-rate for the remainder of the term.
- Billing split: we can invoice partially (pro-rated) if you need the uplift to be recognized across two billing periods; it requires a short PO addendum.

Questions for clarity:
1) Do you want a single uplift that applies immediately for the remainder of the contract, or a staged split (e.g., 40% effective July, additional 20% in Oct)?
2) Any constraints on payment method (PO vs credit card)?

I attached a quick worksheet template (FinTech_Uplift_Worksheet.xlsx) — if you can drop current average monthly tokens into the sheet and indicate preferred split, I can run exact numbers and propose a signed amendment.

Best,

Alyssa / team — attaching a formal pricing appendix with two options:

Option A — Immediate full uplift (60%): blended unit price = $0.00048/token (12% discount vs current list), single invoice when amendment is signed.
Option B — Staged uplift (40% Jul + 20% Oct): blended unit price = $0.00051/token (9% discount vs current list), we issue two pro-rated invoices aligned to the effective dates.

Notes: both options assume the uplift is added as a signed amendment to your existing contract and that the total uplifted commit is guaranteed through Dec 31. We also included a line for a one-time credit (up to $18k) to offset integration timing if you sign before June 15.

I've attached 20270607-uplift-pricing-appendix.pdf for review. Please tell us which option you'd prefer and whether procurement needs the amendment language redlined.
